title: POC Accelerator — 90min Workshop Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact facilitator cheat sheet to run a focused 90-minute customer POC accelerator session. Intended for Solutions Engineering leads running short, outcome-driven workshops where the goal is to validate integration assumptions, prove a small surface area of value, and define the next-phase delivery plan.

Audience:
- 1–2 customer product/engineering reps (technical decision maker + implementation owner)
- 1 customer PM or business stakeholder (optional)
- Redwood: 1 SE lead (facilitator), 1 SE engineer (sandbox support)

Pre-work (send 3 days before):
- Lightweight form: architecture snapshot, primary API consumer flows, success metric(s) for POC (quantitative/qualitative)
- Access: temporary API key for Redwood hosted sandbox OR SSH access to customer staging (if Private), sample dataset (CSV JSON) subset (<= 1000 rows)
- Runbook link and brief checklist for the customer contact: confirm network egress, IP allowlist, and sample credentials

Tech prerequisites (verify before day-of):
- Sandbox verified: demo model loaded, 1 test endpoint responding within 30s
- Seed data validated and sanitized (PII removed)
- Test prompts and expected outputs available in a single document
- Jupyter / Colab link or Postman collection ready for interactive testing

Success criteria for the session (choose 2–3 measurable goals):
- End-to-end request/response validated on customer sample data in session
- Latency and cost estimate for baseline throughput (e.g., 200 qps estimates) discussed and a realistic next-step config proposed
- Customer agrees to a scoped follow-up: e.g., 2-week pilot with quantifiable metrics and an owner assigned

90-Minute Agenda (timeboxed):
0–10 min: Introductions & framing
- Quick intros, roles, and one-sentence goals from each attendee
- Facilitator states scope: what we will and won’t do in 90min; align success criteria

10–25 min: Current state & constraints (customer walkthrough)
- Ask for a 5–7 minute architecture walkthrough: data sources, producers/consumers, security constraints
- Clarifying q's (keep to max 5): authentication, throughput targets, audit/compliance needs

25–50 min: Live integration + smoke test
- SE engineer runs through the integration plan: endpoint, payload example, token/keys
- Execute 3 smoke tests on customer sample data (happy path, edge case, failure mode)
- Capture outputs in shared doc and timestamp results

50–70 min: Results review + performance quick-check
- Discuss observed outputs: correctness, hallucination cases, failure modes
- Quick latency and cost sanity check using Redwood Optimize heuristics (example calc)
- If mismatch, capture root causes and immediate mitigations

70–85 min: Roadmap & next-phase proposal
- Present 3 recommended next steps (pilot scope, tech tasks, evaluation plan)
- Agree on owners, timeline, acceptance criteria
- Risk register: top 3 risks and mitigations

85–90 min: Wrap-up & immediate action items
- Confirm owners for follow-up, 3 deliverables and dates, and whether additional access is needed
- Ask for verbal buy-in (yes/no/maybe) and next meeting cadence

Facilitator cues and script highlights:
- Opening line: "We have 90 minutes to validate one concrete integration and outline a short pilot. By the end you should have a test that runs on your data and a clear next-step."
- When customer drifts: "To keep this useful for everyone, can we park that and capture it as a follow-up?"
- When tech stalls: "We’ll switch to a recorded run and post the logs for deeper debugging—let’s still capture the symptom and any error output now."

Slide skeleton (10–12 slides, quick speaker notes):
1) Title + Goals (note: list the 2–3 success criteria for the session)
2) Agenda + timeboxes (remind people of the 90-minute boundary)
3) Customer context slide (single architecture diagram)
4) POC scope and constraints (what we’ll validate)
5) Integration diagram (endpoints, auth, data flow)
6) Live test plan (cases: happy, edge, fail)
7) Live results (blank before session; fill during)
8) Observations (quality, errors, latency, cost)
9) Recommended pilot options (3 levels: quick win, medium, deep)
10) Acceptance criteria & success metrics
11) Risks & mitigations
12) Next steps, owners, dates

Speaker note examples:
- Slide 4: "We will validate: (A) an end-to-end request using your sample data, (B) one edge case, and (C) an integration resilience scenario (e.g., transient 503)"
- Slide 9: "Tier 1: 2-week smoke pilot, objective: verify E2E correctness over 1k messages. Tier 2: 6-week pilot with throughput tests and model variant comparison."

Live-run checklist (for SE engineer):
- Confirm correct API key and endpoint in environment variables
- Sanity call: curl /health or minimal SDK call -> expect 200 in < 5s
- Run 3 test payloads, capture raw responses, strip timestamps if needed
- Save logs and link to meeting notes (timestamped)

Breakout / hands-on prompts (if you split into two groups):
- Group A: Focus on prompt engineering — try 3 prompt templates on sample and capture output differences
- Group B: Focus on integration resilience — simulate slow upstream, network timeouts, and measure behavior
- Deliverable from each group: 3 bullet findings and one recommended tweak

Evaluation checklist (end of session):
- E2E test executed: yes/no
- Key owner assigned for pilot: name/email
- Pilot scope document agreed: yes/no
- Timeline set (dates): yes/no

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Pitfall: Customer expects full production quality results in 90min. Mitigation: Reiterate scope; show minimal acceptance criteria for demo vs pilot.
- Pitfall: Missing credentials or blocked egress. Mitigation: Have a backup demo dataset and pre-baked video recording of a run.
- Pitfall: Too many stakeholders, signals get fuzzy. Mitigation: Keep decision-maker focused on acceptance criteria and ask for a single owner.

Post-session follow-up template (send within 24h):
- Subject: "Recap + agreed next steps — POC Accelerator (date)"
- Body bullets: summary of what we proved, three observations, agreed pilot scope, owners, dates, and links to logs/artifacts.
- Attachments: filled slide deck (with live results), raw response logs, short how-to for the pilot env setup

Handoff checklist for handover to delivery team:
- Customer contact and primary owner
- Confirmed dataset and access credentials
- Baseline acceptance criteria and success metrics
- Any temporary configuration used in demo (API keys, mock services)

Appendix: quick prompt examples to include in shared doc:
- Classification prompt (binary): "Label the user message as 'support' or 'billing' only. Return single word."
- Summarization prompt: "Summarize the following conversation in <= 25 words, highlight any action items."
- Reranking prompt: "Given a list of candidates, score from 0-1 by relevance to query, return top 3 ids and scores."

Notes to facilitator (final):
- Keep energy high: this format is short—move deliberately and capture everything.
- Use the shared doc as the single source of truth for results and action items.
- If you hit a blocker, convert it into an actionable ticket with owner and due date before the session ends.

End of cheatsheet.
